title: Domain Pocket Prospectus: Live Model Gaps, Buyer Pain Mapping, and Rapid Validation Plan
creator: Priya Nair
description: Purpose: Produce a prioritized prospectus of 6–8 "domain pockets" (vertical + problem combo) where current open models systematically underdeliver for enterprise buyers (latency, privacy, hallucination, domain knowledge, or latency-sensitive RAG). Deliverables: 1) scored pocket list with buyer pain narratives and TAM proxies, 2) synthetic workload probes + pass/fail criteria, 3) rapid validation plan (3-week pilot playbook), 4) engineering feasibility notes and cost delta estimates.
acceptance_criteria: A scored list of >=6 domain pockets with independent rationales and 3 supporting signals each (usage telemetry, customer interviews, public model failure examples)
Synthetic workload probes defined with success thresholds for latency, token-cost, and fidelity (precision@k for QA tasks, hallucination rate under X%)
Pilot plan with instrumentation checklist, required ENG support, and go/no-go decision tree
Cost delta estimates (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for recommended mitigation strategies for each pocket
research_plan: Phase 0: Quick signal harvest (1 week) — combine telemetry slices (embeddings, long-context chat, RAG recall edges), support tickets, and public model bug threads to nominate pockets
Phase 1: Field interviews (1.5 weeks) — 6 targeted customer interviews per pocket (pull from sales CS triage + active accounts) to validate pain and SLA constraints
Phase 2: Synthetic probe design (1 week) — create reproducible workloads and scoring harnesses for model fidelity and latency under realistic token distributions
Phase 3: Pilot blueprint (1 week parallel with ENG scoping) — required infra, batching profile, quantization tradeoffs, and canary routing suggestions
metrics: Signal density: number of independent signals (telemetry, interview, external) supporting a pocket >=3
Pilot pass rate: synthetic probe meets latency and fidelity thresholds >=80%
Customer willingness: >50% of interviewed buyers express readiness to pay for mitigations (quantified as cost delta preference)
Estimated TAM proxy: ARR proxy for pocket (string to capture method: seats * avg spend * adoption fraction)
decisions: Scope limited to enterprise/scale buyers (Mid-market and up) to prioritize SLAs and private deployment economics
Exclude purely consumer-facing UX problems (e.g., chat UI polish) unless they create measurable SLO breaches
Prioritize pockets with clear routing/fallback strategies (can be solved by model variant routing, quantized dedicated tiers, or private deployment)
